correctness.rationale: Structural induction proves all concept extensions are color unions, whose singleton tests are determined by each color multiplicity truncated at two. Nonsingleton points locally cannot satisfy L(C), while singleton pointed colors recover other-color presence at depth one and multiplicity 0/1/2 at depth two using explicit formulas. Global G(C,D) vanishes in the absence of singleton colors; with a singleton anchor, depth-one tests recover all truncated counts. Counting realizable signatures gives every stated closed form; characteristic formulas give all Boolean combinations; 2T-1 is attained and necessary. Independent direct finite-semantic checker passed 1725 pointed signature cases and 48000 random nested-formula comparisons; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Definite descriptions were introduced to support reference without names; the natural attribute-only setting isolates exactly how uniqueness naming and global broadcasts differ. The theorem supplies a full exact invariant, sharp nesting-depth separation, exponential-sized families of pointed theories, corresponding Boolean algebra sizes and optimal model compression; these are not merely routine numeric recalculations, as the single-anchor dichotomy and local point invisibility require separate semantic arguments.
